query: How can we reduce incident resolution time?

per_column.name: incident_category
per_column.rationale: Categorizing incidents (connectivity, email, database) gives a strong grouping axis to compare resolution times across types, directly serving the query. Values are soundly derived from short_description (e.g. 'VPN connection issue' -> connectivity). Note a partial redundancy with the existing 'category' column, slightly lowering usefulness.

per_column.name: incident_location_scope
per_column.rationale: Scope (network_wide vs single_user) is a plausibly useful axis for resolution-time analysis. However groundedness is weaker: 'VPN connection issue' -> network_wide and 'Cannot connect to database' -> application_specific are inferences the terse text does not clearly support, and 'WiFi in sales department' -> department_wide is reasonable while other assignments look asserted beyond evidence.

per_column.name: resolution_status
per_column.rationale: Resolved/open is derivable from state/closed_at fields already present, making it largely redundant with original columns; limited new analytical leverage for reducing resolution time. Values are well grounded (closed_at present -> resolved).

per_column.name: same_technician_assigned_closed
per_column.rationale: Comparing assigned_to vs closed_by is a genuinely useful handoff indicator that could relate to resolution delays. Derivable directly from existing columns, so well grounded; NULLs for open incidents are appropriate.

per_column.name: assigned_technician
per_column.rationale: This restates the existing assigned_to column with essentially the same values, offering little new analytical axis. Values are grounded but trivially redundant.

per_column.name: recurring_incident_pattern
per_column.rationale: Whether an incident is recurring could be useful for targeting systemic causes, but the flag is overwhelmingly 'true' (366/500) and every sample row is marked True with no textual basis. A single short_description gives no evidence of recurrence; these values appear asserted/invented rather than derived.

judge.rationale: The set offers several genuinely useful grouping axes for a resolution-time analysis (incident_category, same_technician_assigned_closed, location scope), but is diluted by redundancy (assigned_technician restates assigned_to; resolution_status echoes state/closed_at). Groundedness is mixed: category and handoff flags read soundly from source, but incident_location_scope over-infers from terse descriptions and recurring_incident_pattern is a near-constant flag with no textual support in any sampled row, indicating hallucination.
